target_customer: Consumers who want to record stories with relatives, paying per interview
problem: People regret not recording relatives' stories; Artifact paired them with professional interviewers and produced podcast style episodes in a private family account.
business_model: Consumer service sold per episode or interview (TechCrunch 2020 listed 175 dollars per episode; a 2022 source lists 149 dollars)
product_category: Personal audio storytelling service with an interviewer marketplace

founders.name: Ross Chanin
founders.background_notes: YC page: grew up in New Jersey, in the Bay Area since 2006. TechCrunch 2020 says he started the company after his grandfather died.

founders.name: Moncef Biaz
founders.background_notes: YC page: born in Morocco, studied in France, moved to the US.

founders.name: George Quraishi
previous_startups: Howler, a soccer magazine he founded and ran for seven years
founders.background_notes: Former writer and editor who taught himself podcasting, per YC page.

exit.reason: Company site says it is shutting down after three and a half years; no reason given on the page read

competitors.name: StoryCorps
competitors.what: Nonprofit oral history recording; Podcast Movement compared Artifact to a commissioned version of it

technical_complexity.rationale: Recording, editing and a marketplace of freelance interviewers; the hard part was operations and quality rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Content stays in customer accounts, which creates some retention, but the service relied on human labor and could be copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response was found; the company shut down on its own.

market_need_then: Chanin's personal loss motivated the idea. TechCrunch 2020 reports an average episode was heard by about 30 people, so demand was for private keepsakes rather than audiences.

branding.domain_note: Operated at heyartifact.com, using a 'hey' prefix rather than an exact artifact.com; no purchase details found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Site copy speaks about family stories and celebrating people in your life

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, The Hustle, Podcast Movement and a Product Hunt launch in September 2020

brand_strength.rationale: A warm, evocative word for keepsakes with launch press, but a common name that collided with Kevin Systrom's unrelated news app Artifact in search results.

outcome_analysis: Artifact raised 500 thousand dollars at launch in 2020 and a reported 5 million dollar seed from GV and Spark Capital in late 2022, then announced it was shutting down after three and a half years. The site read does not state why, and no post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: The 2022 seed is stated by the company's own blog post (heyartifact.com/blog/future-of-artifact) as reported in search results, plus TrendWatching, Dealroom (5.0M seed) and CB Insights (5.13M total); the blog itself returned HTTP 402 and was not opened, so investor names and the pre-seed versus seed split come from the search summary. Exact round date is not given; December 2022 is from TrendWatching. Shutdown date is not stated on the page read (footer shows 2023; interviews could be scheduled until October 31 and stay online through 2024). The StoryCorps source date is approximate. YC page also lists Artifact as a TechCrunch December 2022 item. Not the same company as Kevin Systrom's Artifact news app.
